name: WA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+15 district with a well-funded incumbent seeking re-election
Challenger Mary Silva has raised under $10,000, leaving no visible campaign infrastructure
Prediction markets price DelBene at roughly 97% to win
No general-election polling, but no evidence of a competitive race either
model.rationale: DelBene holds a strongly Democratic district and has raised over $4 million against a challenger who reported only about $8,400, while markets price her win probability near 97%. With no polls showing competition and fundamentals pointing to a blowout, this stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Only a sudden collapse in DelBene's candidacy or an unforeseen scandal could make this competitive; there is no evidence of either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Suzan DelBene enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a western Washington district that leans Democratic by about 15 points. She has built a dominant financial position, raising over $4 million and holding nearly $1 million on hand, while outside spending has flowed only in her favor. Her opponent, Republican Mary Silva, has reported roughly $8,400 in contributions and $1,254 on hand, leaving little sign of a competitive operation.

Prediction markets price DelBene's chances at about 97 percent, and no expert raters flag the seat as contested. With no general-election polling available, the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided money picture. Unless circumstances change dramatically, the seat is expected to remain in Democratic hands by a wide margin.
